#### 1. juvenile primary lateral sclerosis  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.454)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8876198)

**Proposed mechanism:** ALS2 (HGNC:12013) —DISRUPTS→ rab GTPase signaling (GO:0007244); SBF2 (HGNC:11517) —DISRUPTS→ rab GTPase signaling (GO:0007244); rab GTPase signaling (GO:0007244) —LEADS_TO→ Motor neuron degeneration (HP:0007225); rab GTPase signaling (GO:0007244) —LEADS_TO→ Lateral sclerosis (HP:0003724). Loss-of-function mutations in ALS2 (causing MONDO:0011475) and SBF2 (causing juvenile primary lateral sclerosis) both disrupt the rab GTPase signaling pathway. This disruption leads to downstream phenotypes of motor neuron degeneration and lateral sclerosis, respectively.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with loss-of-function mutations in ALS2 or SBF2 that do not exhibit any disruption in rab GTPase signaling pathway components or downstream phenotypes. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the rab GTPase signaling pathway could offer a common therapeutic strategy for both MONDO:0011475 and juvenile primary lateral sclerosis.

Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in SBF2 directly disrupt the ubiquitin-proteasome system, resulting in limb-girdle muscular dystrophy and muscular weakness.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in TRAPPC11 and SBF2 are found to regulate entirely independent cellular pathways that do not converge on the ubiquitin-proteasome system or related protein homeostasis mechanisms, this hypothesis would be falsified. Specifically, if evidence shows TRAPPC11 mutations primarily affect lysosomal function and SBF2 mutations primarily affect DNA repair without a shared downstream consequence on protein degradation. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in the coding regions of TRAPPC11 and SBF2 in gnomAD that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of protein homeostasis and degradation pathways in these distinct genetic disorders could reveal common therapeutic targets for muscular dystrophies and neurodevelopmental disorders. Modulating the ubiquitin-proteasome system or upstream protein trafficking could offer a unified therapeutic strategy.
